To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rumen epithelium transcriptome data from two independent experiments with sheep were highly correlated and identified a set of metabolic genes associated with rumen CH4 production and CH4 yield and muscle cell junction genes associated with ruminal MRT and CH4 yield.
we identified the expression of genes involved in lipid/oxo-acid metabolism and muscle cell junctions as the most likely contributors to the host effects on CH4 yield in sheep.
the expression of genes in the ketone synthesis pathway and muscle junction genes in the rumen epithelium are associated with variation in CH4 yield in sheep.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the host influence on ruminal methane production and has identified several potential causal genes.
the identification of host genes and pathways involved in rumen fermentation that are associated with variation in CH4 production.
understanding the mechanisms by which host factors affect the efficiency of CH4 production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the host rumen wall transcriptomes are associated with rumen microbial metabolism and CH4 production and that the expression of a subset of genes in the host rumen muscle may be associated with rumen function.

the rumen wall transcriptomic data from AUS and NZ sheep experiments were highly correlated, and the expression of the metabolic genes and the muscle cell junction genes were associated with CH4 production and CH4 yield.
rumen epithelial metabolic genes and muscle cell junction genes are associated with CH4 production and CH4 yield, respectively, and the expression of the two sets are negatively correlated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rumen wall is a complex tissue that is responsive to diet and that the rumen microbial metabolism and the host muscle contraction rate both influence the rumen environment and CH4 production.

rumen epithelial cell cycle and metabolic functions are correlated with rumen acetate and butyrates concentrations and CH4 phenotypic variation, whereas the muscle cell junctions genes are associated with CH4 yield.
the rumen wall transcriptomic data provide a valuable resource for the study of rumen function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the host is an important factor in determining the efficiency of ruminants in converting feed into CH4.
host genetics and physiology can influence CH4 production and CH4 yield through rumen epithelial metabolism and muscle contraction rates.

the rumen epithelium is a complex organ that is responsive to both the host and rumen microbes, and that the rumen wall transcriptomics can provide insights into the host-microbe interactions and the molecular basis of host effects on rumen functions.
